A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HybridMQA work, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures. The core sections can be matched reliably. v2 includes supplementary Sections 6–8 absent from the supplied v1, allowing comparison of the newly documented material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, cross-dataset generalization tests, component ablations, and GradCAM analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and additionally reports fusion, augmentation, and viewpoint/batch-size ablations, gMAD comparisons, and further GradCAM examples.

M1.justification: The encoders, GCN, aligned rendering, cross-attention, quality regression, and losses remain unchanged in Section 3. The supplement newly documents CMDM-specific graph initialization and training viewpoint dropout for previously reported evaluations; it does not establish these as revisions to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Nehme et al., SJTU-TMQA, TSMD, and CMDM, retaining the same cross-dataset tasks. Supplementary analyses use existing datasets. Point-cloud quality assessment remains a proposed future application.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eleven MQA comparators, and Table 2 retains LPIPS and Graphics-LPIPS. Graphics-LPIPS also remains the gMAD comparator already identified in v1. The supplementary fusion comparisons are component ablations.

E3.justification: Tables 5–7 add targeted experimental configurations: fusion replacements, augmentation removal, and combinations of 2/4/6 viewpoints with batch sizes 2/4/8. The principal cross-validation design and SRCC/PLCC metrics remain unchanged. Newly disclosed training settings and TSMD exclusions do not establish revisions to the earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained representation and model-branch ablations, v2 supplies direct cross-attention comparisons against five fusion alternatives, augmentation ablations, and viewpoint/batch-size sensitivity tests. It also supplies the previously referenced gMAD comparison and additional mesh and cross-attention GradCAM cases, substantially expanding the available diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five-fold cross-validation and median performance across five experiments. v2 adds no seed information, confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises TSMD-trained SRCC/PLCC: HybridMQA changes from 0.857/0.825 to 0.846/0.811, Graphics-LPIPS from 0.801/0.795 to 0.784/0.773, and LPIPS SRCC from 0.711 to 0.712. HybridMQA remains highest. Tables 5–7 and Figures 8–11 add substantial ablation and qualitative results. Tables 1, 3, and 4 retain their values. The unexplained Table 2 revisions do not establish a same-setting performance deterioration.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–11 are retained. The supplement introduces experimental configurations and implementation information, without new theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: a hybrid full-reference colored-mesh assessment framework, aligned feature rendering, geometry-texture interaction modeling, and superior performance and generalization. Additional evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: The supplement explains the memory rationale for viewpoint dropout and interprets its relationship with attainable batch size. The conclusion makes the prospective point-cloud extension more concrete by specifying graph-edge construction. Existing viewpoint-weighting and full-graph memory limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 6 supplies substantial missing reproducibility information: dataset counts and TSMD exclusions, Adam and cosine scheduling, 15 epochs, batch size 8, loss weight 1, V100 32GB hardware, augmentation parameters, CMDM handling, training viewpoint dropout, and logistic fitting for PLCC. The abstract also replaces a future implementation-release promise with a project website address.

R1.justification: v2 adds MM-PCQA and LMM-PCQA citations when discussing future point-cloud extensions. The related-work sections and positioning against existing mesh-quality approaches otherwise remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and narrative are retained, with localized wording refinements in the introduction, method descriptions, and conclusion. The supplement organizes the added material into setup, ablation, and qualitative-results sections; the main paper is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5–7 and Figures 8–11, including a gMAD comparison panel and extensive GradCAM grids. Original Figures 1–7 remain visually equivalent, with minor formatting changes. The new displays substantially expand the paper's visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies essential implementation details and supplementary evidence that v1 references but does not include. Table 5 directly tests the central cross-attention contribution, while Tables 6–7 clarify augmentation and memory/batch-size tradeoffs. These additions substantially improve reproducibility and support for the method. The unexplained Table 2 revisions and continued absence of uncertainty estimates limit assessment, but do not outweigh these gains.
